_read_me: The roster of occasions worth a post. Edited by hand; read by the weekly
scheduled task. Adding an occasion here is all it takes for the task to
start watching for it.
TRADITION. The first field to get right, and the one that has already gone
wrong once. Most Indian observances are kept on different days by different
communities and regions, and the web returns whichever one is loudest.
Vishwakarma Puja is the example: eastern India keeps it on Kanya Sankranti
in September, and the north keeps it the day after Diwali, which is the one
a Delhi steel trade observes. A search for 'Vishwakarma Puja 2026' returns
17 September and nothing at all about that split.
So every entry states whose observance it follows, and the task resolves
the date FOR THAT TRADITION or produces nothing. An entry whose tradition
reads UNCONFIRMED is not ready to be used and the task must skip it and
say so.
DATES. Most of these move every year, so this file does not pretend to be
a calendar. 'fixed' entries carry a month-day that never changes. Others
carry the month they fall in, plus a 'hint' for years someone has already
looked up. The task resolves the real date from a live source every week
and must cite where it got it. If the resolved date and the hint disagree,
the task stops and says so rather than posting on the wrong day.
BRANDS. An occasion is not automatically both firms'. Vishwakarma Puja is
a workshop's day; Metal Dock marks it and Dockfinity has no business doing
so. List only the brands that should actually post.
ANGLE. The one thing this firm can say about this day that a greeting-card
company cannot. It is the whole reason for posting. If the angle reads
like it could sit under any logo, the post is not worth making.
STILL MISSING. This roster is festivals only. The trade dates that Metal
Dock buyers actually care about - the Budget and its effect on import
duty, financial year end, DGTR hearing dates, the steel and housewares
expos - are not here yet, and neither are Dockfinity's launch windows and
conference dates. Those were agreed as part of this pipeline on 15 Sep
2026 and are the next thing to add.

occasions.name: Vishwakarma Puja
occasions.tradition: North India, the day after Diwali (Govardhan Pratipada). This is the household's own observance. NOT the Kanya Sankranti date in mid-September, which is how Bengal, Odisha, Bihar and Jharkhand keep it and which is what a plain search returns.
occasions.about: The day the tools, the machines and the workshop itself are cleaned, garlanded and rested. In the north it falls the day after Diwali, alongside Govardhan Puja.
occasions.angle: The only day in the year that is about the machines rather than the people or the money. A supplier that actually runs a shop floor can say something here that a brand posting a stock diya cannot.

occasions.name: Dussehra / Vijayadashami
occasions.tradition: North India. The tenth day of Sharad Navratri.
occasions.about: The tenth day, after the nine of Navratri. Traditionally the day new work and new ledgers begin.
occasions.angle: Shastra puja - the day the instruments of one's trade are honoured. For one firm that is steel and machines, for the other it is what it builds.

occasions.name: Dhanteras
occasions.tradition: Pan-Indian trade custom; the North Indian observance is the relevant one here.
occasions.about: The first day of the Diwali five. The day metal is bought - traditionally a vessel, which is why it is the single biggest utensil-buying day of the Indian year.
occasions.angle: The trade's own festival, and the one day the whole country does what Paatra sells the rest of the year. Say something true about why the custom is metal, not why to buy ours.

occasions.name: Diwali / Lakshmi Puja
occasions.tradition: North India, Lakshmi Puja on the Amavasya of Kartik.
occasions.about: The main day of the five.
occasions.angle: Everyone posts on Diwali, which is exactly why a generic one is invisible. Take the year that is ending in this house or this shop, not the lamps.

occasions.name: Bhai Dooj
occasions.angle: Listed so the task does not treat it as missing. No brand posts unless someone adds one - a family day does not need a supplier's greeting.

occasions.name: Makar Sankranti
occasions.tradition: Solar, so the date barely moves. Kept across the north on 14 January.
occasions.about: The solar turn, when the sun enters Makara. One of the few Indian festivals on a near-fixed date, because it follows the sun rather than the moon.
occasions.angle: The year's first turn, and the start of the buying season that runs to the wedding months.

occasions.name: Republic Day
occasions.angle: A manufacturing floor and a software company are both downstream of what a republic guarantees. Say that plainly or do not post - the flag alone is filler.

occasions.name: Holi
occasions.tradition: North India. Rangwali Holi, the day after Holika Dahan.
occasions.angle: The shop shuts. Say something about the pause, not the colours.

occasions.name: Mahavir Jayanti
occasions.tradition: UNCONFIRMED - Digambar and Svetambar keep the same day here, but confirm before first use.
occasions.about: The birth of Mahavira, the twenty-fourth tirthankara.
occasions.angle: Ahimsa and aparigraha read differently from inside a trading business than from outside one. That tension is the post.

occasions.name: Akshaya Tritiya
occasions.tradition: Pan-Indian trade custom; North Indian observance.
occasions.about: Considered an auspicious day to buy metal; second only to Dhanteras for the trade.
occasions.angle: Same caution as Dhanteras. Explain the custom, do not run an offer.

occasions.name: Independence Day
occasions.angle: Only worth posting with something specific - what this firm makes here, and where the steel or the software actually comes from.

occasions.name: Kshamavani / Micchami Dukkadam
occasions.tradition: UNCONFIRMED - Svetambar keep Samvatsari at the close of Paryushan; Digambar keep Kshamavani at the close of Das Lakshana, about ten days later. In 2026 the post went out on 16 September, the day after Samvatsari. Which sampradaya this household follows has not been written down, so the task must not resolve this date on its own.
occasions.about: Uttam Kshama, the first of the Das Lakshana, and the asking of forgiveness that closes Paryushan.
occasions.angle: Done in 2026: the Prakrit glossed word by word, because almost nobody prints what miccha and dukkada actually mean. Keep the discipline, change the copy.
